scripts.//dev: Every installed transport, and every write to hardware refused; :write allows them — read the hardware warning in the README. Simulated devices are added as such, and take writes either way.
scripts.dev: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server" "npm run web"
scripts.dev:write: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:write" "npm run web"
scripts.//start: The whole thing, fully enabled: writes to hardware ALLOWED, client bundled in production mode and neither side restarting on file changes. This is the dangerous one — read the hardware warning in the README.
scripts.start:prod: npm run free-ports && concurrently -n server,client -c magenta,cyan "npm run server:prod" "npm run web:prod"
scripts.//server: The server alone, without Metro. Read-only, like dev; :write allows writes to hardware.
scripts.//broker: The MQTT broker stations connect to. It runs detached and outlives the server; the server starts one when none is running. See docs/BROKER.md.
scripts.//client: The app alone, against whichever server it is pointed at.
scripts.//build:web: The production web build, as the web container serves it: a static single-page app in client/dist.
scripts.//users: Accounts, from a shell on the server — for when nobody can log in. See server/src/auth/cli.ts.
scripts.//free-ports: Not 1883. That is the MQTT broker, which runs as its own process precisely so that restarting the server does not drop the station; killing it here would undo that on every npm run dev. Use npm run broker:stop to stop it on purpose.
scripts.//test:e2e: The app end to end: the web build against a read-only server of its own, every device simulated (e2e/). Builds the app first; E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 reuses client/dist.
scripts.//typecheck: Every workspace, the e2e suite, and the shared packages as every place runs them: no Node or Bun types (tsconfig.shared.json, docs/PLAN-SHARED-CORE.md).
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present && tsc --noEmit -p e2e && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.shared.json
scripts.//check:architecture: The dependency rule, the product-identifier ratchet (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 7) and a current device registry. Add -- --update to record an improvement.
scripts.//knip: Files, exports and dependencies nothing uses, and dependencies used but not declared (knip.jsonc says what runs and why).
scripts.//gen:devices: Writes the app's registry of device types, protocols, transports and screens from the installed packages (client/src/generated/registry.ts). Run it after adding a package; CI checks it is current.
scripts.//config: Checks a configuration file against what is installed, or prints its JSON Schema: npm run config -- check kraftverk.yaml. See docs/CONFIG.md.
scripts.//new: Starts a device type, protocol or transport that already keeps its contract. See docs/ADDING-A-DEVICE.md.
